title: The story everyone repeats. Pac-Man was renamed to stop vandals scratching an F onto arcade
description:
Pac-Man was renamed to stop vandals scratching an F onto arcade cabinets. Repeated by CNN, Wikipedia, and countless retellings; but no Namco executive, document, or interview has ever been found saying this.

22 May, Japan. Namco's original name for the character, from 'paku-paku'; the Japanese sound for a mouth opening and closing.

The shape came from a missing slice of pizza. "I was eating a whole pizza while thinking about a game themed on eating," he told Game Informer in 2020, "and I came up with the design after looking at the pie with a slice taken out."

October. Published the US version under the changed name; Pac-Man; an Americanisation, not a confirmed scandal dodge.

coin-operated plays between 1980 and 1999, per Guinness World Records; the highest-grossing arcade game ever.

Sources:
- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pac-Man - established the Japan release date (22 May 1980), the original name 'Puck Man', the paku-paku etymology, and the October 1980 Midway US release under the changed name.
- https://www.thrillingtalesofoldvideogames.com/blog/pac-man-hockey-pucks-paku-paku - a dedicated investigation confirming the paku-paku etymology via the official Pac-Man Museum and Chris Kohler's 'Power Up', and establishing that the vandalism-rename story is attributed inconsistently across retellings, with no confirmed source on the Japanese side of Namco.
- https://gameinformer.com/classic/2020/06/19/pac-mans-creator-on-the-legacy-pizza-and-the-future - a direct, on-record quote from creator Toru Iwatani confirming the pizza-slice inspiration for the character's design.
- https://www.guinnessworldrecords.com/world-records/98519-highest-grossing-arcade-videogame - the official record: approximately 10 billion coin-operated plays and $3.5 billion in cumulative earnings between 1980 and 1999, making Pac-Man the highest-grossing arcade video game of all time.
